findings.message: This is an instance fix for the duplicate-write class. A retry now checks the stored result only inside the service transaction, and it does so after authorize() and safeParse() have run again. Any step before that check can fail on the retry: authorize, validate, or a registry or tool pre-check before the service. That failure then closes the card as `failed`, and the user is told "This couldn't be done… Nothing was changed" even though the write committed on the first attempt. Fix: look the key up first. Do it at the top of `call` before authorize, or in confirmAction before registry.call. Return the stored outcome if there is one. Add a variant test where the retry hits a refusal after a committed first attempt.
findings.scenario: Confirm card → create_proposal commits, then the reply is lost (ActionFailedError retry:true). An admin removes Maya's delivery:proposal:create grant. Maya clicks Add it again → authorize fails → ForbiddenError (retryable=false) → the card is settled as 'failed' and the note says 'Nothing was changed' while the proposal row exists.

findings.message: retryable() replaced the PERMANENT set, but it only covers error classes that were given `retryable = false` in this diff. The old checks are gone. ZodError was in the set, and so was any error carrying code 'forbidden', 'invalid_input' or 'not_found' that is not a ToolError. Both are now treated as retryable. A permanent failure therefore leaves the card open with "Try again or cancel" for good. Fix: keep the code/name checks, or mark every permanent error class, and extend the chat outcome test table with ZodError and code-only errors.
findings.scenario: A chat write tool whose input fails a zod parse inside the tool (ZodError has no `retryable` flag) → ActionFailedError(retry:true). The card stays open, every retry fails the same way, and the card is never closed as failed.

findings.message: Nothing checks that the idempotency key was actually used. withIdempotency covers only the first defineService call in the scope. If a tool writes outside defineService, or makes a second service call after the first, the later writes are not covered by the key. confirmAction still reports such a retry as safe (retry:true), and a cancel 'wins' while the write still runs. Fix: return the scope's `used` flag from withIdempotency (or check it afterwards). If the key was never taken, or the tool made more than one write, fail closed: treat the outcome as unknown and do not offer a blind retry.
findings.scenario: A write tool whose run calls service A and then service B. The reply is lost after both commit. Retry → A returns its stored result and B runs again, so the B write is duplicated. Separately, cancel claims the key, the confirm runs a non-defineService tool, the write happens, and the card says it was cancelled.

findings.message: The 'Cancel wins' race holds the confirm at a gate before registry.call, so the cancel commits before the service transaction even begins. The claimed guarantee that a cancel and a confirm can't both win depends on cancel's claimKey blocking on the confirm's uncommitted key row. No test ever has the cancel arrive while the write transaction is open. Fix: put the gate inside spec.run (after claimKey, before commit), start cancelAction, release the gate, and assert three things: the cancel throws NotPendingError('confirmed'), exactly one row exists, and the card is recorded as confirmed.
findings.scenario: Change claimKey in the service so it runs after spec.run (no lock held during the write). The current test stays green, but a cancel landing mid-write would then claim 'cancelled' and the write would commit as well.

findings.message: settleKey stores the service's raw `out.result` in core.idempotency. The audit row goes through redact() by sensitivity class; this copy skips that. The table has no retention rule, and amax_app has no delete grant, so rows can never be pruned. Any personal or sensitive fields in a write result (pay, health, bank, candidate) are copied unredacted into a core table and kept forever, against the 002/032 classification and retention requirement. Fix: store only what a replay needs (for example ids or keys) or redact by spec.sensitive. Add a TTL or retention job and the delete grant it needs.
findings.scenario: A chat-confirmed write whose result includes a `pay`-class field → the value is persisted unredacted in core.idempotency.outcome with no expiry.

findings.message: The exactly-once and cancel-wins guarantee only holds if the tool's first defineService call is the write, and if the tool makes no other write. Nothing checks this. Case 1: a write tool that calls no defineService at all (for example the packages/mcp admin writes that skip the pipeline) never takes the key. Then a cancel claims the key, the confirm still writes, and settle() quietly returns because the card is no longer pending. confirmAction then returns success, so the UI says 'done' while the conversation records 'cancelled'. Case 2: a tool whose first service call is a read, or a tool that makes two writes. The key goes to the first call only. On a retry, every other write runs again. Fix: give withIdempotency a way to report whether the key was taken, and have confirmAction fail closed (ActionFailedError, not done) when registry.call returns without using it. Either reject chat write tools that make more than one write, or give each nested write its own derived key. When settle() finds the card already cancelled after a write committed, record it as confirmed, not as nothing.
findings.scenario: A chat write tool that calls no defineService: the user clicks Add it, then Cancel while the call is running. The cancel inserts {cancelled:true}, the write still commits, confirmAction returns the result and the card shows done, but chat.conversation.decided says cancelled. Or: a tool calls a read service and then the write. The reply is lost and the user retries. The read takes the key, the write runs again, and there are 2 rows.

findings.message: A replayed result is the JSON round-trip of the original. Dates become strings and undefined fields are dropped, so a retry returns a different shape from the first call to the same service.
findings.scenario: A service result holding a Date → the first call returns a Date, a retry returns an ISO string.

findings.message: The old permanent() list was replaced with a `retryable === false` flag on selected classes. Two variants the old code covered are dropped. (1) ZodError was in PERMANENT but has no flag, so it now counts as retryable. (2) The old check also read a `code` of forbidden, invalid_input or not_found on any error, and only ToolError got the flag. retryable() also looks only at the top-level error, so a permanent error wrapped as `cause` reads as retryable. Each of these leaves the card open with 'Try again' forever, when it should close as failed. Fix: keep a single classifier that covers the names, the code values and the cause chain. Add a table test with ZodError, an error carrying a code, and a wrapped ForbiddenError.
findings.scenario: A tool's input fails a zod parse and throws a ZodError. confirmAction throws ActionFailedError(retry:true). The card shows 'That didn't work… Try again', and every retry fails the same way, where before this change the card closed as failed.
